newsitem.title: USA: Portland plans $657 million port expansion.
newsitem.headline: Portland plans $657 million port expansion.

text.p: The Port of Portland is planning a $657 million expansion, adding three terminals for grain and containers and a six-track rail yard, port officials said Friday.
The new facilities would be built on Hayden Island, a four-mile island in the Columbia River north of the port's Rivergate Industrial District.
The island now includes residential and commercial developments on its east end, but the west end is vacant.
The Port of Portland is the largest element of the Columbia River grain-export district, second largest in the world after New Orleans.
The other Columbia River export terminals are the Washington state ports of Vancouver, Kalama and Longview.
A decision on the plan is expected from the Port Commission at its April meeting. It could take 25 years to complete the project, but the first phase could be ready for cargo by 2003.

Project manager Jim Laubenthal said the plan anticipates that rising exports of U.S. grain will continue to be high, and that some mid-Canadian wheat shippers may use Portland elevators because their subsidy on rail shipments has been canceled.
One major Canadian exporter, Canpotex, is already building a high-speed potash terminal in Portland for Pacific Rim trade.
Port spokesman Daryl Buttice said the plan will be financed by combined private and public funding as the various elements are built.
He said the first terminal is expected to cost about $111 million, and the other two will cost about $368 million. The rail yard will cost about $56 million. Other infrastructure also will be added.
Most construction materials will be moved in by barge, to reduce road damage. The final design will include greenways and wetlands for wildlife habitat.
